meta.description: Constraint-based metabolic modeling (COBRA). FBA, FVA, gene knockouts, flux sampling, SBML models, for systems biology and metabolic engineering analysis.

scientific_integrity.detail: Accurate representation of COBRA methodology and COBRApy library capabilities; no fabricated methods

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for constraint-based metabolic modeling and systems biology applications

methodological_ground.detail: Based on established COBRA methodology, FBA theory, and validated solver implementations (GLPK, CPLEX, Gurobi)

code_usability.detail: All code examples are syntactically correct with proper imports and context managers for safe state management

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of COBRA capabilities including FBA, FVA, knockouts, sampling, gapfilling, and model building with excellent reference organization

reliability.note: Strong troubleshooting guidance covering infeasible solutions, slow optimization, and unbounded solutions; minor: could expand error recovery patterns

performance_context.note: Well-organized documentation (497 lines main + comprehensive workflow reference) with clear sections and progressive disclosure

agent_usability.note: Excellent 'When to Use This Skill' section with specific triggers; clear capability boundaries; comprehensive workflow examples with operational notes

human_usability.note: Clear installation with version pinning; multiple workflow examples; solver configuration guidance; best practices for context managers

security.note: Good practices for file I/O with user confirmation before writing outputs; no credential risks; minor: lacks guidance on handling proprietary models

maintainability.note: Excellent structure with version 1.1, clear license (GPL-2.0), comprehensive reference files, deprecation notices, and external resource links

agent_specific.note: Strong composability with allowed-tools specified; clear integration with solvers; operational notes for performance; minor: could specify output format schemas

key_strengths: Exceptional coverage of COBRA methodology with comprehensive examples for FBA, FVA, knockouts, sampling, and production strain design
Outstanding reference organization with separate workflow files providing detailed step-by-step implementations
Excellent use of context managers for safe state management, preventing common model manipulation errors
Strong performance awareness with operational notes about genome-scale model runtime and solver selection
Clear scope boundaries between bundled models, remote BiGG models, and custom SBML files with network requirements
